about: The `town_meeting_votes` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2022 only.

rows.subject: Accept the town's annual departmental and committee reports
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT (to Pass Over as written reports have been accepted).

rows.subject: Authorize FY23 revolving funds for town departments and boards
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to re -authorize the revolving funds for certain town departments, boards, committees, agencies or officers for spending limits as printed in the Annual Town Meeting warrant (as listed below):

rows.subject: Transfer funds to pay prior year bills
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to transfer $500.00 from Free Cash for payment of prior year expenses.

rows.subject: Amend the FY2022 budget with line-item transfers
rows.quote: VOTED (Yes-123, No-1) to transfer from line #4/Liability Insurance the sum of $28,275.60; transfer from #5/Workers Compensation the sum of $5,340.00; transfer from line #6/Group Health Insurance the sum of $116,826.72; transfer from line #13/Reserve Fund the sum of $20,000.00;

rows.subject: Fund the first year of the AFSCME municipal employees union contract
rows.quote: VOTED (Yes-120, N0 -6) to transfer from Article 6 of the 5/1/21 Annual Town Meeting and Article 1 of the 11/16/21 Special Town Meeting, line #13A/Salary Reserve the sum of $15,303.51 to fund the first year of the FY22 -FY23 Collective Bargaining Agreement dated July 1, 2021 – June 30, 2023

rows.subject: Fund the FY2023 Capital Plan
rows.quote: VOTED (Yes-122,No-45) to raise and appropriate the sum of $967,725.00; transfer from Free Cash the sum of $983,034.39; transfer from Article 28 of the 5/7/16 Annual Town Meeting the sum of $20,582.40; transfer from Article 6 of the 5/5/18 Annual Town Meeting the sum of $1,168.29;

rows.subject: Reorganize DPW to create a separate Facilities and Grounds Department
rows.quote: VOTED (Yes -136, No -28) to approve the Administrative Organization Plan as presented by the Town Manager and as provided for in Article 5, Section 1 (b) of the Town Charter:

rows.subject: Transfer funds to the Stabilization Fund
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to transfer from Free Cash the sum of $100,000 to the Stabilization Fund.

rows.subject: Transfer funds to the Special Purpose Stabilization Fund
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to transfer from Free Cash the sum of $450,000 to the Special Purpose Stabilization Fund.

rows.subject: Fund the OPEB Trust Fund
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to transfer from Free Cash the sum of $266,696 and transfer from Sewer Enterprise Retained Earnings the sum of $656.00 to the OPEB Trust Fund established at the November 30, 2010 Special Town Meeting.

rows.subject: Fund the Sewer Enterprise Fund for FY2023
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to appropriate from Sewer Enterprise revenues the sum of $853,112.53; transfer from the Sewer Capital Reserve Stabilization Fund the sum of $20,000.00; transfer from the Sewer Reserve Capacity Fund the sum of $20,962.00;

rows.subject: Transfer funds to the Sewer Capital Reserve Stabilization Fund
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to transfer from Sewer Enterprise Retained Earnings the sum of $35,548.86 into the Sewer Capital Reserve Stabilization Fund.

rows.subject: Fund the Solid Waste Disposal Enterprise Fund for FY2023
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to appropriate from Solid Waste Disposal Enterprise Revenues the sum of $302,000 to operate the Solid Waste Disposal Program.

rows.subject: Fund the Water Enterprise Fund for FY2023
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to appropriate from Water Enterprise Revenues the sum of $25,000 to operate the Water Department.

rows.subject: Fund the PEG Access (cable) Enterprise operating and capital budgets for FY2023
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT vote to appropriate from PEG Access and Cable Related revenues the sum of $152,477.00; and appropriate from PEG Access and Cable Related Enterprise retained earnings the sum of $11,090.00; for a total appropriation of $163,567.00

rows.subject: Appropriate cemetery lot sale proceeds for cemetery upkeep
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to appropriate the sum of $10,000 from the Sale of Cemetery Lots account to be used for the care and improvement and embellishment of the Town Cemeteries.

rows.subject: Fund cleanup of solid waste materials at the Woodruff Property
rows.quote: VOTED (Yes-164, No-7) to transfer $100,000 from Free Cash to remove and dispose of solid waste materials and restore the work area to prior natural conditions at the property known as the Woodruff Property, known as and numbered 104 Fairview Road, as shown on Assessor's Map 080, Lot 021,

rows.subject: Fund demolition of the old Primary School building at 30 School Street
rows.quote: VOTED (Yes 145; No 18) with amendment to appropriate from Free Cash $250,000 for the demolition of the building at the property known as the old Primary School, 30 School Street, shown on Assessor's Map 071, Lot 076.

rows.subject: Add and reclassify positions in the Salary Administration Plan
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to amend Chapter 70 of the Town's General Bylaws, entitled "Salary Administration Plan," Schedule A, as follows: the position of Council on Aging Assistant Meal Site Manager to be added and assigned to Grade 3;

rows.subject: Adopt the FY2023 salary schedule and fund resulting wage increases
rows.quote: VOTED (Yes-142, N0-4) to replace the current Salary Schedule in Chapter 70, Section 70-8.A, the Salary Administration Plan of the General Bylaws, with a FY 2023 Salary Schedule as recommended by the Personnel Committee as printed in the Annual Town Meeting Warrant Booklet,

rows.subject: Amend the Salary Administration Plan bylaw
rows.quote: VOTED (Yes-155, No-78) (with amendment to 70 -19, section C – italicized) to amend the General Bylaws, Chapter 70, entitled "Salary Administration Plan" as depicted in the handout entitled "5/7/22 ATM Article 22: Salary Administration Plan Bylaw Amendments",

rows.subject: Amend various sections of the General Bylaws
rows.quote: ARTICLE 24 VOTED (Yes-171, No-4).

rows.subject: Amend the Sewer Bylaw's sewer service area and waiver provisions
rows.quote: VOTED  (Yes -147, No -33)  2/3rds Declared.( with Amendments to Section 10 “Waivers”) to amend the Lunenburg Sewer Bylaw as follows:

rows.subject: Amend the FY2023 budget with additional departmental line-item appropriations
rows.quote: VOTED (Yes-136, No-5) (94 needed for 2/3rds Majority) to raise and appropriate the sum of $73,000 as follows: to line #22/Town Manager Expense, the sum of $10,000.00; to line#28/Assessors Administration, the sum of $45,000.00; to line #35/Planning Board, the sum of $5,000.00;

rows.subject: Appropriate funds to pay prior year bills
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to raise and appropriate $1,804.54 for payment of prior year expenses.

rows.subject: Fund the first year of the Police Officers union contract
rows.quote: VOTED (Yes-127, No-11) to transfer from Article 8 of the May 7, 2022 Annual Town Meeting, line #13A/Salary Reserve, the sum of $16,000.00 to fund the first year of the FY23-FY25 Lunenburg Police Officers Collective Bargaining Agreement dated July 1, 2022 – June 30, 2025

rows.subject: Fund engineering and design work for Marshall Park
rows.quote: VOTED (Yes-124, No-24) to raise and appropriate the sum of $184,000 for the property known as the Marshall Park, 100 Chestnut Street, shown on Assessor's Map 060, Lot 018,

rows.subject: Transfer funds to the Special Purpose Stabilization Fund
rows.quote: Article 5 was PASSED OVER

rows.subject: Transfer funds to the Sewer Reserve Capacity Stabilization Fund
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to see if the Town will vote to transfer from available funds $1,645.60 into the Sewer Reserve Capacity Stabilization Fund.

rows.subject: Transfer funds to the Sewer Inflow/Infiltration Stabilization Fund
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to see if the Town will vote to transfer from available funds $9,900.00 into the Sewer Inflow/Infiltration Stabilization Fund.

rows.subject: Accept a state retirement-credit provision for reserve and call police/fire personnel
rows.quote: VOTED (Yes-119, No-7) to accept the provision contained within M.G.L. c. 32 § 4(2)(b) written as such:

rows.subject: Add positions to the Salary Administration Plan
rows.quote: VOTED UNANIMOUS CONSENT to see if the Town will vote to amend the Code of Lunenburg, Chapter 70, Section 70 -8.A, entitled "Salary Administration Plan”, Schedule A, as follows: the position of Administrative Assistant - IT to be added and assigned to Grade 8;

rows.subject: Add a bylaw limiting Town Meeting's ability to amend capital appropriation articles
rows.quote: Article 10 was DEFEATED.

rows.subject: Amend the Protective Bylaw use table for motels in the Commercial District
rows.quote: VOTED (Yes-91, No-24) (77 needed for 2/3rds majority) to amend the Code of Lunenburg, Section 250 -4.1G, which is a Section of the Protective Bylaw entitled “Use Table,” by changing 4.1K(10) Motel in the Commercial District from “Y” to “SP-Z”.

rows.subject: Override the Architectural Preservation District Commission's denial for the Ritter Memorial Building
rows.quote: Article 12 was DEFEATED.

rows.subject: Rezone a portion of 199 Massachusetts Avenue to Commercial District
rows.quote: VOTED (Yes-95, No -10) (70 Needed for 2/3rds Majority) to amend the Zoning Map by rezoning a portion of the land located at 199 Massachusetts Avenue from Residence A to Commercial District so the entire lot is in the Commercial District,

rows.subject: Move the Annual Town Meeting and Town Election dates to April
rows.quote: Article 15 was DEFEATED.
